root_cause.text: The NPU_SET_IFM_REGION handler incorrectly used a 0x7f bitmask (allowing values 0–127) instead of 0x7 (0–7) for extracting the region index, leading to out-of-bounds writes into the `region_size[]` array (sized to 8) during command stream validation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff changes `st.ifm.region = param & 0x7f;` to `st.ifm.region = param & 0x7;`. The CVE description confirms that `region_size[]` and `output_region[]` are both sized to `NPU_BASEP_REGION_MAX` (8), and that all other similar assignments use `param & 0x7`. The description further notes that `feat_matrix_length()` and `calc_sizes()` use the region index directly as an array subscript, so a value >7 results in a heap write of up to 1016 bytes past the start of `region_size[]`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect bitmask for region field in NPU_SET_IFM_REGION command to limit to 3 bits (0-7) instead of 7 bits (0-127).
intent_record.what: Changed the bitmask for the region field in the NPU_SET_IFM_REGION case from 0x7f (7 bits) to 0x7 (3 bits).
intent_record.how: The region value is now masked to only the lower 3 bits (0-7) instead of the lower 7 bits (0-127), restricting the range of valid region identifiers.

grouping_result.intent: Fix incorrect bitmask for region field in NPU_SET_IFM_REGION command to limit to 3 bits (0-7) instead of 7 bits (0-127).

relevance_review.reason: The group's changes directly fix the incorrect bitmask that caused the out-of-bounds vulnerability described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: The bitmask 0x7f allows region values from 0 to 127, but region_size[] array has only 8 entries (index 0-7). Assigning a region >=8 leads to out-of-bounds write when later used as an array index.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the NPU_SET_IFM_REGION handler, 'st.ifm.region = param & 0x7f;' allows region values 0-127, while the region_size[] array is sized for 8 entries (as indicated by other region handlers using & 0x7). This enables out-of-bounds writes to info->region_size[region] in functions like dma_length and feat_matrix_length. The fix would be to change the mask to 0x7.
